choices.text: Escaping `%` when it appears in a `:!` argument
choices.why: It stands for the current file name, which is also what makes `:w !sudo tee %` work.

choices.text: Avoiding `:r !` in favour of copying the text in
choices.why: It would work, and it gives up a genuinely useful command.

prompt: You have five minutes on an unfamiliar production machine. Which two commands tell you what an editor-opening tool will start?
hint: One reads the environment, the other resolves the fallback.

choices.why: Between them: what is set, and what the fallback resolves to on this distribution.
That tells you what is installed, not what will be opened.
The first is git's own setting; the second names your login shell.
Those are configuration files for editors you have not chosen yet.

prompt: Which of these is a fair summary of what this lesson asks of you?
hint: Count the commitments it actually makes.

choices.text: Learn vim properly; the other two are for people passing through
choices.why: The lesson refuses that framing in as many words.

choices.text: Be able to leave any of the three, and be able to work in one
choices.why: Four vim keys for the machine you did not choose, and one editor you are fluent in.

choices.text: Standardise your team on one editor and document it
choices.why: A reasonable policy, and not something this lesson argues for.

choices.text: Stop editing files on servers and use a configuration manager
choices.why: It says to arrange that, and it also says every such system fails into an editor.
